subject: Byline exchange: short case study + press permission in return for deal concession
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sara Klein <sara.klein@aperturehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Byline exchange: short case study + press permission in return for deal concession

Sara —

Really enjoyed our product deep-dive this morning. Aperture’s rollout plan looks like a great fit for Redwood’s Dedicated offering. As we discussed on the call, the procurement team is asking if we can include a 15% pricing concession on the first-year commit if Aperture agrees to a short co-authored case study + a byline and permission to use Aperture’s logo in Redwood marketing and a short customer quote.

High level proposal:
- 15% one-year discount on the Dedicated commitment (applies to committed capacity only)
- Aperture to approve a 1–1.5 page byline/case blurb and allow logo + one short quote (non-sensitive, pre-approved copy)
- Redwood to run the asset after Aperture review and approval; no product-level technical details or PHI 

If that’s acceptable, I can route to our deal desk and product marketing to get a draft and a simple publicity matrix over to you. Can you confirm who on your side will own approvals (legal or marketing)?

Appreciate it — I’ll hold off on the formal discount until we have the publicity guardrails locked.

Best,
Jonas
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: publicity-matrix.xlsx (stub)

From: Sara Klein <sara.klein@aperturehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Aperture Health Legal <legal@aperturehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Byline exchange: short case study + press permission in return for deal concession

Jonas —

Thanks for the summary and the offer. Aperture is open to cooperative marketing but we have a few non-negotiables from a compliance perspective:
- No PHI or patient-level metrics in any public assets.
- Any quote must be pre-approved by our comms team (I’ll loop them if needed).
- We prefer a 6–9 month embargo window after go-live before mass distribution.

Legal is copied (legal@aperturehealth.com) — they will send redlines for any publicity language. On our side, I’ll own approvals with support from legal and marketing. If you send a draft byline and a short publicity matrix that calls out placement, audience, and timing, we’ll review quickly.

Sara
Head of Partnerships | Aperture Health
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Byline exchange: need deal-desk OK + exec sign-off for non-standard publicity clause

Team —

Forwarding Aperture’s reply. They accept in principle but Legal will send redlines; they want a 6–9 month embargo and strict no-PHI language. Deal details: Aperture is pushing for a 15% first-year concession. I’m asking deal desk to tentatively approve 15% for exec escalation, with the following conditions:
- Concession only applies to committed Dedicated capacity (no credits on overage).
- Redwood retains final approval on copy; Aperture signoff required pre-publish.
- No product-level metrics or screenshots that would reveal customer PII/PHI.

Attached: draft-byline-case-study.pdf (marketing sketch) and publicity-matrix.xlsx. Please advise if we should move to formal exec approval — legal concern flag below.

Thanks,
Jonas

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Byline exchange: need deal-desk OK + exec sign-off for non-standard publicity clause

Jonas —

Thanks for the context and the attachments. Key legal/brand ops concerns from our side:
- The requested embargo (6–9 months) is fine, but we should avoid an exclusivity clause that restricts our ability to promote product capabilities elsewhere.
- If Aperture’s legal proposes long approval timelines or unlimited review cycles, that nullifies the marketing value. We should cap approval to two review rounds and a 7-business-day turnaround per round.
- Regarding the concession: 15% feels high if Aperture insists on extended review cycles and restrictions on content. I recommend we counter at 12% with the cap on review rounds and a clause that the discount is conditional on Aperture publishing the asset within 9 months of final approval.

I’m happy to approve the 12% as Deal Desk lead; anything above that needs direct exec sign-off. I’ve attached an annotated publicity matrix and highlighted the clauses I want removed.

Lauren
Director, Deal Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redlines_publicity_matrix.xlsx (stub)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Exec escalation: Aperture Health publicity swap — approval request for concession above deal-desk threshold

Rishi —

Quick summary: Jonas has a near-term close with Aperture Health. Customer is willing to provide a co-authored byline + logo + short quote in exchange for a first-year concession. Deal Desk (Lauren) is comfortable up to 12% provided we cap review cycles and tie the concession to a publication timeline. Sales is asking for 15%.

Requesting exec sign-off to approve up to 15% for this deal under the following conditions:
- Discount applies only to committed Dedicated capacity and expires after year one.
- Publication must follow our no-PHI clause; Redwood retains final approval on copy.
- Approval rounds limited to two; 7 business days per review.
- If Aperture fails to publish the agreed asset within 9 months of final sign-off, the concession is rescinded (credit reversal clause).

I’ve attached the draft case blurb and the publicity matrix. Legal expects to send final redlines; redlines from Aperture will be shared as they arrive. Given the revenue velocity on this account, sales is asking we move quickly.

Thoughts?

—Vivek
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec escalation: Aperture Health publicity swap — approval request for concession above deal-desk threshold

Team —

Approve up to 15% under the conditions Vivek laid out, with two additions:
1) Add a clause that any customer quote referencing ARR/financial metrics must be limited to percentage improvements only (no raw revenue numbers).
2) Marketing to include a one-time paid social boost (to be covered by Redwood marketing budget) only if Aperture co-authors and approves usage within 9 months.

Jonas — move forward with the 15% concession and send Aperture a clean draft that includes the review caps and the credit reversal clause. Lauren, please add the two additions to the standard publicity agreement and circulate for signature.

Rishi
Chief Revenue Officer | Redwood Inference
